items.info: Control Column. Ensures free and correct movement of the flight controls before flight.
items.label: Control Locks

items.info: Left side panel. Prevents the aircraft from rolling during prep.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Various Panels. Ensures no electrical loads are active when turning on the battery, preventing sparks or damage.
items.label: All Switches

items.info: Left and Right Side Panels. Verifies all electrical systems have power available and no faults have tripped them.
items.label: Circuit Breakers

items.info: Lower Left Panel. Turning it on protects the engine from ice and debris but raises ITT, so it stays off unless needed.
items.label: Inertial Separator

items.info: Overhead Panel. Ensures the engine will draw fuel from both wing tanks evenly.
items.label: Fuel Selectors

items.info: Upper Right Panel. Reduces electrical and bleed air load prior to starting the engine.
items.label: Ventilation/AC

items.info: Lower Panel. Reduces engine load and ITT temperatures during the starting sequence.
items.label: Bleed Air Heat

items.info: Center Pedestal. Keeps the engine under normal FCU (Fuel Control Unit) governing instead of manual fuel metering.
items.label: Emergency Power Lever

items.info: Center Pedestal. Sets elevator, rudder, and aileron trim to neutral or takeoff positions for safe departure.
items.label: Trim Controls

items.info: Push in to let fuel reach the engine. It is a separate control from the firewall valve, and both must be in.
items.label: Fuel Cutoff

items.info: Center Console. Prevents radar emissions from injuring ground personnel or draining the battery.
items.label: Weather Radar

items.info: Left Panel. Powers the aircraft for the fuel quantity and flap checks that follow.
items.label: Battery Switch

items.info: Instrument Panel. Confirms sufficient fuel for the planned flight.
items.label: Fuel Quantity

items.info: Instrument Panel. The fuel senders are sensitive to lateral G-force and to how level the aircraft sits, so an apparent imbalance can be false. Check fuel levels when any discrepancy shows.
items.label: Fuel Balance

items.info: Center Console. Lowers the flaps so their tracks and hinges can be inspected during the exterior walkaround.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Left Panel. Turn on, then off. Confirms the heating elements work to prevent icing in flight.
items.label: Pitot/Stall Heat

items.info: Left Panel. Disconnects battery power to save charge while completing the exterior walkaround.
items.label: Battery Switch

items.info: Exterior. Ensures all external surfaces, components, and covers are safe and ready for flight.
items.label: Preflight Inspection

items.info: Cabin.
items.label: Passenger Briefing

items.info: Cabin. Secures the main entry and cargo doors so they do not open in flight.
items.label: Cabin Doors

items.info: Left side panel. Prevents the aircraft from rolling during prep.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Cabin. Confirm pilot and passengers secured.
items.label: Seats & Harnesses

items.info: Various Panels. Verifies equipment is still off before electrical power is introduced.
items.label: All Switches

items.info: Left Panel. Arms the ignition system to fire automatically during the start sequence.
items.label: Ignition Switch

items.info: Left and Right Side Panels. Confirms all breakers are set for normal operations.
items.label: Circuit Breakers

items.info: Overhead Panel. Ensures continuous fuel flow from both wing tanks.
items.label: Fuel Selectors

items.info: Push the CABIN HEAT MIXING AIR valve in before starting and keep it in for flight. Left out, it can overheat the cabin vent, which disables bleed air heating. GND-PULL is only for extra heat on the ground below 85% Ng.
items.label: Cabin Mixing Air

items.info: Center Pedestal. Must be stowed in normal to prevent uncommanded engine surges.
items.label: Emergency Power Lever

items.info: Center Pedestal. Sets the fuel control to minimum for a safe, low-temperature engine start.
items.label: Power Lever

items.info: Center Pedestal. Full forward. Places the propeller in low pitch for minimum resistance during start.
items.label: Prop RPM Lever

items.info: Center Pedestal. Keeps fuel shut off until the engine compressor reaches sufficient speed.
items.label: Fuel Condition Lever

items.info: Push in to let fuel reach the engine. It is a separate control from the firewall valve, and both must be in.
items.label: Fuel Cutoff

items.info: Pull handle on the lower throttle quadrant. Pulled out, it closes the firewall valve and cuts the engine off from fuel. A warning tone sounds when the engine has no fuel supply.
items.label: Firewall Valve

items.info: Left Panel. Powers the starter relay and engine instruments.
items.label: Battery Switch

items.info: Center Console. Retracts flaps to the normal position for engine start and taxi.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Overhead Panel. Recessed gauge. The cylinder is normally serviced to 1,850 PSI and depletes with use and altitude.
items.label: Oxygen Pressure

items.info: Confirms every annunciator lamp works.
items.label: Annunciators

items.info: Red test button next to the annunciator panel. The fire siren sounds and the red ENGINE FIRE annunciator lights.
items.label: Fire Detector

items.info: Left Panel. Warns ground personnel that the engine is about to start.
items.label: Beacon

items.info: Left Panel. Verifies the battery has a minimum of 24 volts to ensure a successful start without overheating.
items.label: Bus Volts

items.info: Exterior. Visually confirm no people or equipment are near the prop.
items.label: Propeller Area

items.info: Left Panel. Activates the auxiliary fuel boost pump. AUX FUEL PUMP ON light should illuminate, confirming the pump is running.
items.label: Fuel Boost Switch

items.info: Left Panel. The IGNITION ON light should illuminate and oil pressure should start rising. Wait for Ng to stabilize above 12% before moving the fuel condition lever.
items.label: Starter Switch

items.info: Center Pedestal. Introduce fuel at Ng 12%. Monitor ITT closely: 1090°C is the limit, and only for 2 seconds at most.
items.label: Fuel Condition Lever

items.info: Confirms fuel is reaching the engine.
items.label: Fuel Flow

items.info: Instrument Panel. Confirms the engine has accelerated to a self-sustaining idle speed.
items.label: Ng Stable 52%

items.info: Left Panel. Disengages the starter motor once the engine is running smoothly.
items.label: Starter Switch

items.info: Confirms the starter has disengaged.
items.label: Starter Engaged Annun

items.info: Left Panel. Connects the generator to the electrical bus. Verify the GENERATOR OFF light extinguishes.
items.label: Generator Switch

items.info: Left Panel. Verify positive load. Confirms the generator is charging the battery and powering the aircraft.
items.label: Generator Amps

items.info: Read on the volt/amp meter.
items.label: Battery Charging Current

items.info: Green range is 4.5-5.5 inHg up to 15,000 ft.
items.label: Suction

items.info: Left Panel. Turns the auxiliary fuel boost pump off once the engine is running. The fuel boost pump annunciator should extinguish.
items.label: Fuel Boost Switch

items.info: Set the remote compass controller mode switch to SLAVE. The synchroscope should show a white line centered between the + and - marks. The copilot DG is not driven by the remote compass and must be set by hand.
items.label: Remote Compass

items.info: Left Panel.
items.label: Nav Lights

items.info: Left Panel. Powers up the radios, GPS, and flight displays after engine voltage is stable.
items.label: Avionics 1 & 2

items.info: Upper Right Panel. Adjusts environmental controls for crew and passenger comfort.
items.label: Cabin Heat/Vent

items.info: Instrument Panel. Sets the local barometric pressure so the altimeter reads the correct field elevation.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: Center Console. Programs the flight plan and communication frequencies for departure.
items.label: Avionics/GPS

items.info: Center Console. Sets the initial heading and altitude bugs for the climb.
items.label: Autopilot

items.info: Center Console. Inputs the assigned squawk code and keeps it on standby until near the runway.
items.label: Transponder

items.info: Lower Left Panel. Set to ON on loose surfaces or icing conditions to prevent engine damage.
items.label: Inertial Separator

items.info: Left Panel. Illuminates the taxiway and makes the aircraft more visible.
items.label: Taxi Lights

items.info: Lower Left Panel. Frees the wheels so the aircraft can move.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Rudder Pedals. Test during initial roll to ensure directional control and stopping ability.
items.label: Brakes & Steering

items.info: Instrument Panel. Verify airspeed, attitude, and heading indicators respond correctly.
items.label: Flight Instruments

items.info: Confirm the synchroscope line is centered and the HSI heading agrees with the magnetic compass.
items.label: Remote Compass

items.info: Lower Left Panel. Keeps the aircraft stationary during engine run-up and final checks.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Control Column and Pedals. Check for full and free movement to ensure nothing is binding.
items.label: Flight Controls

items.info: Instrument Panel. Verifies no red X's or flags on the primary displays.
items.label: Flight Instruments

items.info: Instrument Panel. Final check that the altimeter is set to the current local pressure.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: Overhead Panel. Verifies fuel will feed from both tanks for maximum safety during takeoff.
items.label: Fuel Selectors

items.info: Instrument Panel. The fuel senders are sensitive to lateral G-force and to how level the aircraft sits, so an apparent imbalance can be false. Check fuel levels when any discrepancy shows.
items.label: Fuel Balance

items.info: Instrument Panel. Final confirmation of adequate fuel for the flight.
items.label: Fuel Quantity

items.info: Confirms it is fully pushed in before takeoff.
items.label: Fuel Cutoff

items.info: Left Panel. Sets the boost pump to its normal position for flight.
items.label: Fuel Boost Switch

items.info: Center Pedestal. Advance the power lever smoothly to approximately 400 ft-lb torque. Hold at this power for the Inertial Separator check.
items.label: Power Lever

items.info: Lower Left Panel. With the power lever at 400 ft-lb, set the inertial separator ON and check that ITT increases. Then set it OFF.
items.label: Inertial Separator

items.info: Center Pedestal. Set the power lever for 1800 RPM, then press and hold the overspeed governor test button. Propeller RPM should drop to 1750 ±60 RPM. Return the power lever to idle. At 1800 RPM the sim's static thrust can overpower the brakes. The test can also be run in flight, at RPM very close to 1750, because RPM drops very quickly when the button is pressed.
items.label: Overspeed Governor

items.info: Turn on and check that generator load increases, then turn off.
items.label: Pitot Heat

items.info: Turn on and check that generator load increases, then turn off.
items.label: Windshield Anti-Ice

items.info: Turn on and check 20-24 amps on the propeller ammeter, then turn off.
items.label: Propeller De-Ice

items.info: Turn on and watch the airframe de-ice annunciator cycle, then turn off.
items.label: Airframe De-Ice

items.info: Set the heading bug 30 degrees left, engage heading mode and watch the yoke move. Repeat with the bug 30 degrees right, then test the disconnect and set the autopilot for climb.
items.label: Autopilot

items.info: Left Panel. Backs up the starter-generator. It takes part of the load when the generator load passes a preset value and the engine is above idle.
items.label: Standby Alternator

items.info: Left Panel. With the volt/amp meter on ALT, the standby alternator should show zero amps. With the generator carrying 30-60 amps, move the generator switch to TRIP: the standby alternator load should turn positive. Then move the generator switch to RESET.
items.label: Standby Power

items.info: Center Pedestal. Check the manual electric pitch trim for correct direction and movement in both nose-up and nose-down directions.
items.label: Pitch Trim

items.info: Center Pedestal. Elevator, aileron, and rudder trims must be in the takeoff band to avoid heavy control forces.
items.label: Trim

items.info: Left Panel. Set to ON for wet runways, heavy precipitation, or icing to prevent flameouts.
items.label: Ignition Switch

items.info: Lower Left Panel. Set to ON for icing conditions or FOD-prone runways.
items.label: Inertial Separator

items.info: Left Panel. Activate pitot, stall, and prop heat if flying into visible moisture near freezing.
items.label: Ice Protection

items.info: Center Console. 10 degrees for a normal takeoff, 20 degrees for a short field.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Confirm the CABIN HEAT MIXING AIR valve is pushed in for flight.
items.label: Cabin Mixing Air

items.info: Center Pedestal. Increases idle RPM so the engine responds faster to power lever movements.
items.label: Fuel Condition Lever

items.info: Center Console. Activates altitude reporting so air traffic control can track the flight.
items.label: Transponder

items.info: Left Panel. Increases visibility before entering the active runway.
items.label: Strobes

items.info: Left Panel. Further increases visibility to other aircraft during the takeoff roll.
items.label: Landing Lights

items.info: Lower Left Panel. Releases the brake set for the run-up before takeoff power is applied.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Center Pedestal. Advance smoothly to takeoff torque: 1865 ft-lb maximum, ITT 805°C maximum. Torque rises as the aircraft accelerates and can pass the redline, so keep watching it during the roll.
items.label: Power Lever

items.info: Control Column. Pull back gently to lift the nose wheel off the runway.
items.label: Rotate

items.info: Center Console. Fully retract the flaps at 95 KIAS.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Center Console. Confirm the indicator shows 0 degrees to avoid overspeeding the flaps.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Left Panel. No longer needed once airborne.
items.label: Taxi Lights

items.info: Left Panel.
items.label: Landing Lights

items.info: Lower Left Panel. Turn it off once clear of icing or dirty air. It raises ITT while on.
items.label: Inertial Separator

items.info: Left Panel. Manage de-icing boots and heat based on outside air temperature and visible moisture.
items.label: Ice Protection

items.info: Center Pedestal. Max performance climb: 1865 ft-lb with ITT below 765°C. Enroute climb: 1865 ft-lb with ITT below 740°C.
items.label: Power

items.info: Center Pedestal. 1900 RPM for a max performance climb, 1600-1900 RPM for an enroute climb.
items.label: Prop RPM Lever

items.info: Instrument Panel. Best rate of climb speed (Vy). Best angle of climb speed (Vx) is 72 KIAS.
items.label: Climb Speed

items.info: Instrument Panel. Set to 29.92 inHg or 1013 hPa when climbing through the transition altitude.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: Center Pedestal. Set prop 1600-1900 RPM and torque for cruise. Do not exceed ITT, Ng, or torque limits; cruise ITT limit is 740°C.
items.label: Cruise Power

items.info: Lower Left Panel. Set to ON if entering clouds with temperatures near freezing.
items.label: Inertial Separator

items.info: Left Panel. Monitor for ice buildup on the wing struts and activate boots as needed.
items.label: Ice Protection

items.info: Instrument Panel. The fuel senders are sensitive to lateral G-force and to how level the aircraft sits, so an apparent imbalance can be false. Check fuel levels when any discrepancy shows.
items.label: Fuel Balance

items.info: Lower Left Panel. Set to ON for icing conditions or when descending through precipitation.
items.label: Inertial Separator

items.info: Left Panel. Keep heat on if flying through clouds or rain at low temperatures.
items.label: Ice Protection

items.info: Left Panel.
items.label: Landing Lights

items.info: Center Pedestal. Any setting in the 1600-1900 RPM green range.
items.label: Prop RPM Lever

items.info: Center Pedestal. Pull back to start the descent.
items.label: Power Lever

items.info: Cabin signs on for the descent.
items.label: No Smoking/Seatbelt

items.info: Instrument Panel. Adjust to the destination airport's barometric pressure when crossing the transition level.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: Cabin.
items.label: Seats & Seatbelts

items.info: Left Panel. Ensures the aircraft is highly visible to the control tower and other traffic.
items.label: Landing Lights

items.info: Lower Left Panel. Keep ON for icing conditions or if the runway is unpaved.
items.label: Inertial Separator

items.info: Overhead Panel. Verifies the engine has access to all remaining fuel.
items.label: Fuel Selectors

items.info: Instrument Panel. The fuel senders are sensitive to lateral G-force and to how level the aircraft sits, so an apparent imbalance can be false. Check fuel levels when any discrepancy shows.
items.label: Fuel Balance

items.info: Center Pedestal. Should still be in HIGH IDLE from lineup, so the engine responds faster to power lever movements.
items.label: Fuel Condition Lever

items.info: Center Pedestal. Final check that the propeller is fully forward for maximum thrust or drag.
items.label: Prop RPM Lever

items.info: Center Console. First stage of drag configuration for the approach. The sim limits every flap setting to 125 KIAS; the real aircraft allows 175 KIAS up to 10 degrees.
items.label: Flaps 10°

items.info: Center Console. Further slows the aircraft and improves forward visibility over the nose. The sim limits every flap setting to 125 KIAS; the real aircraft allows 150 KIAS from 10 to 20 degrees.
items.label: Flaps 20°

items.info: Center Console. Final landing configuration. 125 KIAS is the limit from 20 to 30 degrees in both the sim and the real aircraft.
items.label: Flaps Full

items.info: Control Column. Press the yoke disconnect button. The AP annunciator flashes for five seconds and a tone sounds.
items.label: Autopilot

items.info: Center Console. Double check the indicator to ensure maximum lift and drag are established.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Center Pedestal. Final check that the propeller is fully forward for maximum thrust or drag.
items.label: Prop RPM Lever

items.info: Center Pedestal. Reduce power at the threshold. Do not use Beta range in flight to avoid severe aerodynamic forces.
items.label: Power Lever

items.info: Center Pedestal. Pull back past idle into beta after touchdown. Return to idle before 25 knots.
items.label: Power Lever

items.info: Rudder Pedals. Toe brakes.
items.label: Brakes

items.info: Left Panel. Prevents blinding other pilots and ground crew while taxiing.
items.label: Strobes

items.info: Left Panel. Illuminates the taxiway.
items.label: Taxi Lights

items.info: Left Panel. Reduces electrical load and avoids blinding ground personnel.
items.label: Landing Lights

items.info: Center Console. Retracts flaps to reduce lift and increase weight on the wheels for better braking.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Left Panel. Prevents heating elements from burning out on the ground and saves electrical power.
items.label: Ice Protection

items.info: Center Pedestal. Reduces engine RPM and taxi speed.
items.label: Fuel Condition Lever

items.info: Center Console. Prevents harmful radiation exposure to ground crews.
items.label: Weather Radar

items.info: Center Console. Takes the transponder off the active air traffic network, though some airports require it left ON.
items.label: Transponder

items.info: Lower Left Panel. Secures the aircraft at the parking stand.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Left Panel. Protects delicate radios and displays from voltage spikes when the battery is turned off.
items.label: Avionics 1 & 2

items.info: Left Panel.
items.label: Standby Alternator

items.info: Left Panel. Secures the auxiliary fuel pump.
items.label: Fuel Boost Switch

items.info: Various Panels. Removes all environmental electrical and bleed loads prior to engine shutdown.
items.label: Bleed Air/Vent/AC

items.info: Center Pedestal. Let ITT stabilize for at least 1 minute to allow engine temperatures to cool evenly.
items.label: Power Lever

items.info: Center Pedestal. Pull fully aft to stop propeller rotation quickly and prevent the blades from acting as a sail in the wind.
items.label: Prop RPM Lever

items.info: Center Pedestal. Shuts off fuel to the engine, causing it to spool down.
items.label: Fuel Condition Lever

items.info: Left Panel. Turns off all exterior and interior lights to prevent draining the battery.
items.label: All Lights

items.info: Left Panel. Completely depowers the aircraft.
items.label: Battery Switch

items.info: Overhead Panel. Shuts off fuel from both wing tanks.
items.label: Fuel Selectors

items.info: Shuts off the oxygen supply.
items.label: Oxygen

items.info: Left off for the next start.
items.label: Inertial Separator

description: A legendary go-anywhere platform engineered to conquer unpaved strips and remote missions.
